angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 250,459 km at 27.65 pc = 0.12 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 36.1663 +/- 0.0283 mas (same row, RUWE 1.34): 27.65 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.36001 +/- 0.030968 solar radii from Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-129 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract): 250,459 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.360031 +/- 0.067677 solar masses from Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-129 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3459.09 +/- 89.05 K from Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-129 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-129 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-129.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.882, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
